# Two balls that cover a ball, one-limb center

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_split_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

Two balls that together cover the ball $X$ of center $c$ and radius $r$, one each half:

$$[c - r, c] \subseteq [c_a - r_a, c_a + r_a], \qquad [c, c + r] \subseteq [c_b - r_b, c_b + r_b].$$

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `X.split()` | `Ball<T, 1>` | `Split<Ball<T, 1>>` | covers $[c - r, c]$ and $[c, c + r]$; the parts are not claimed inside $X$, nor smaller than $X$; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode; not `constexpr` |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- the ball of center $c$ and radius $r$ is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- The two parts, of centers $c_a$ and $c_b$ and radii $r_a$ and $r_b$, are canonical balls.
- If the ball $X$ of center $c$ and radius $r$ is empty, both parts are; if it is the whole line, both are the whole line.
- Otherwise every real number of $[c - r, c]$ is a member of the first part, and every one of $[c, c + r]$ a member of the second.
- Not claimed: that the parts are inside $X$, nor that their radii are close to $r/2$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_split_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeBallSets.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeBallSets.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions ball_split_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `ball_split_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the point c plus the balls (-h, q) and (h, q), q = max(h, r - h), by the proved ball sum (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_split_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_split_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`ball_add_1_full`](ball_add_1_full.md).

```
# Two balls that together cover a ball with a one-limb center (milestone2.md, "One enclosure
# interface", "Hull, intersection and split of balls"): the first contains [c - r, c], the second
# [c, c + r]. Each is the sum ball_add_1_full of the point c and a ball of center -h or +h, h =
# RN(r/2), and of radius q = max(h, r - h) (r - h is exact): c + [-h - q, -h + q] contains [c - r, c]
# since q >= h and h + q >= r. The whole line and the empty set are returned twice, as they are (a
# ball cannot be a half-line, so splitting the whole line makes no progress). The page's listing
# negates hs = select(fr, h, 0), whose first arm is the product h, which the generator refuses (no
# fused result negated, directly or through a select); here -h is its own product, of the negated
# radius, nh = select(fr, prod(-r, 1/2), 0): the same value, rounding to nearest being symmetric.
# Not claimed: that the halves are inside X, nor that their radii are close to r/2 when r is near the
# underflow range (each has the H of a ball sum).

h        = prod(r, const up(1/2))
nr       = neg(r)
hn       = prod(nr, const up(1/2))
g        = sub(r, h)
mg       = lt(h, g)
q        = select(mg, g, h)
fr       = lt(r, const inf)
hs       = select(fr, h, 0)
nh       = select(fr, hn, 0)
ws       = select(fr, q, 0)
cs       = select(fr, c, 0)
(a0, a1) = ball_add_1_full(cs, 0, nh, ws)
(b0, b1) = ball_add_1_full(cs, 0, hs, ws)
ca       = select(fr, a0, c)
ra       = select(fr, a1, r)
cb       = select(fr, b0, c)
rb       = select(fr, b1, r)
```

## Measured

No stored brute-force run has judged this kernel yet.

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
